content.text: Home Resources IT Glossary IT Glossary Technology is full of acronyms and jargon. We believe you shouldn't need a computer science degree to understand what your IT company is talking about. Here's our plain English guide to the terms that matter for your business. EDR (Endpoint Detection & Response) Is antivirus enough? The risk: Traditional AV misses 60% of modern attacks. What we do: EDR watches for behaviour, stopping ransomware instantly. Application Control (Ringfencing) Who controls what runs? The risk: Users can accidentally run malware or bad scripts. What we do: We block everything by default. Only approved apps can run. RMM (Remote Monitoring & Management) How do you fix things so fast? The risk: Waiting for things to break causes downtime. What we do: We fix issues in the background before you notice them. SIEM (Security Information & Event Management) Who watches the logs? The risk: Hackers can hide in your logs for months without you knowing. What we do: SIEM collects logs from everywhere and alerts us to anomalies. MDM (Mobile Device Management) What if a phone is lost? The risk: Company data on a lost phone is a GDPR breach. What we do: We can remotely wipe corporate data without touching personal photos. VPN (Virtual Private Network) Do I need a VPN to work remotely? The risk: Without encryption, data on public WiFi was exposed to eavesdroppers. What we do: Modern cloud apps are encrypted by default. VPNs are now mainly for accessing on-premise servers. ZTNA (Zero Trust Network Access) What replaces traditional VPN? The risk: VPNs grant full network access once connected - one compromised device exposes everything. What we do: Zero Trust verifies every connection, granting only the specific access needed, continuously. Want to Go Deeper? Each of these technologies has a dedicated explainer page with detailed information on how it works, why it matters, and how we deploy it for your business.
